findings.claim: All 14 phenomenon rows are PHENOMENON_SPECIFIC_MODEL_REPLAYED with a specific model, observable, negative control, and falsifier.
findings.failure_mode: The falsifier text is boilerplate repeated across every row: a finite model flips the claimed observable without runner rejection. That is a harness-level schema, not a phenomenon-specific falsifier. The matrix therefore closes broad phenomenon coverage without naming row-specific countermodel conditions, state changes, or executable falsifier cases.
findings.required_repair: Replace the generic falsifier fields with row-specific falsifier conditions tied to each model_card observable and runner case IDs; keep PHENOMENON_SPECIFIC_MODEL_REPLAYED only where the row has a concrete executable falsifier or an explicitly scoped non-executable falsifier boundary.

findings.claim: P012 / OC133-NOSEND-001: release governance is explained through claim -> Lean theorem/proof sheet -> semantic finite case -> negative control -> falsifier.
findings.failure_mode: The no-send model card cites formal/lean/OC133V12.lean and describes a Lean theorem/proof-sheet route, but the theorem inventory and proof ledger contain only T133-* theorem rows, and OC133V12.lean contains no no-send theorem. The finite no-send checks point at JSON manifests, not Lean. This is theorem-route theater for a governance state machine.
findings.required_repair: Either add an OC133-NOSEND theorem inventory row, proof sheet, and Lean lemma over the owner-approval state machine, or reclassify P012 as manifest-only governance evidence with a manifest-specific negative control and falsifier.

findings.claim: P005 / T133-HYBRID: OC explains operators in non-smooth proof and rewrite domains.
findings.failure_mode: The model card says typed update with smooth chart optional and hybrid guard/reset, while the executable finite cases only check primitive=typed_update, smooth_requires_chart, and hybrid_guard_reset_checked. There is no proof-state carrier, rewrite transition, chart-absence derivative request, or proof/rewrite observable, despite the proof sheet claiming a proof-replay rewrite example.
findings.required_repair: Add an executable proof/rewrite model case with theorem states, rewrite steps, no smooth chart, derivative-request rejection, and a smooth-chart negative/control comparison; wire the runner to those fields instead of the primitive string.

findings.claim: P002 / T133-ID: OC explains death, residue, and rebirth without identity equivocation.
findings.failure_mode: The row is bound only to T133-ID and FM-T133-ID-POS, whose executable model contains morphism=rebirth, identity_invariant_preserved=false, and classified_as_identity=false. It does not encode a death event, residue production/preservation, or a residue-to-new-live rebirth construction. Death coverage exists under T133-OMEGA-STATUS but is not part of this model card route.
findings.required_repair: Split P002 into identity/rebirth and death/residue model cards, or bind it to both T133-OMEGA-STATUS and T133-ID with one executable lifecycle model containing death, residueOf, rebirthOf, new live state, identity invariant, and paired negative controls.

findings.claim: T133-OMEGA-STATUS: live status, death, residue, and rebirth are distinct typed predicates and morphism classes.
findings.failure_mode: The promoted Lean subset declared_death_blocks_live has the shape death=true -> live=false -> live=true -> False. It assumes live=false instead of deriving it from death or a lifecycle consistency invariant, and it does not machine-check residue/rebirth non-interchangeability. The theorem inventory promotes this as the machine-checked subset for the broader status claim.
findings.required_repair: Define and prove a lifecycle consistency invariant that derives death=true -> live=false and separately proves residue/rebirth/identity separation, then update the theorem inventory and finite model checks to point at the strengthened theorem or demote the claim scope.
